newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks higher but fading in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks higher but fading in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were higher but fading in volatile late trade on Wednesday as the closely watched electronics sector, buoyed by overnight Wall Street and Nasdaq rallies, continued to rise, brokers said.
With 45 minutes left, at 0315 GMT, the benchmark stock index was up 43.18 points or 0.45 percent at 9,593.58, off an intraday high 9,694.28. Turnover was heavy at T$137 billion.
The heavily weighted electronics had rebounded 2.76 percent, echoing big rises in the U.S. markets and regaining more than half of the 4.16 percent lost in a dramatic selloff on Tuesday.
"Wall Street and Nasdaq overnight rallies have helped push the electronic sector," Alex Yang of National Securities said.
The Dow Jones industrials on Tuesday surged 155 points to 8,062, while the high-tech driven Nasdaq composite rebounded from recent profit-taking to gain 27.63 points to 1,563.86.
Brokers said the ex-bonus issue of United Microelectronics Electronics also lent strength to electronic sector.
United Micro, Taiwan's second largest micropchip maker, surged through the session after going ex-bonus and was up T$6.5 at T$116 in late trade, brokers said.
Motherboard giant Asustek was up T$30 at T$548.
